dimensions.evidence: "caused by loss of one working copy of the CDKL5 kinase... random X-inactivation silences the healthy copy in about half of neurons"; "duplications spanning CDKL5 cause neurobehavioural problems, so overshooting is a real liability"; appendix: skewed-XCI females "unaffected or mildly affected"; exon skipping rejected as pathogenic.

Appendix enumerates 12 mechanisms with existence/alleles/discovery-burden columns, but enhancer/eRNA-directed transcriptional upregulation is absent (only a cis-NAT "antagoNAT" row), and the main answer offers just three options: variant splice correction, poison exon, 3'UTR.

"no CDKL5 poison exon with meaningful neuronal flux has been described"; exon 17 "in-frame, ~10% of brain transcripts, so it is not a poison exon"; exon-11 cryptic "<5%"; gated: "stopped if... no non-productive CDKL5 event carrying at least 10% of pre-mRNA flux"; exon-16-skip hazard control included.

"zorevunersen gives CDKL5 only chemistry, intrathecal dosing, safety and regulatory precedent — zero expectation of fold-upregulation"; "Its efficacy rests on a validated, highly-used SCN1A non-productive exon; CDKL5 has no demonstrated poison exon at all."

Rich landscape (UX055 IND slip, Biogen AAV exit, Elaaj ELJ-101, split-dCas9 E6del preprint, Angelman Phase 3 miss, fenfluramine GEMZ), but CAMP4's RAP platform and the SYNGAP1 ~1.5-fold NHP analogue — the closest clinical analogue — are entirely absent.

"deep brain nuclei see more than tenfold less drug than cortex" and a monkey biodistribution study are proposed, but as a "follow-on" test, while appendix asserts "Delivery to CDD neurons is largely solved by plain intrathecal ASO" and "brainstem... well covered" — contradicting nusinersen autopsy data.

Has NMD arm ("decay-inhibition arms"), long-read isoform fractions, EB2 pS222 function, specificity and kill criteria. But single genotype (c.2376+5G>A only), cortical neurons only, "nucleofection" rather than gymnotic uptake, and no single gate discriminating the candidate handles.

Main answer cites "a genome-wide screen did not nominate CDKL5" as a pillar of the kill criterion, yet the appendix records "the Pigini poison-exon preprint (preprint PDF returned HTTP 429 twice, not read)" while elsewhere asserting "a 2026 brain poison-exon atlas with no CDKL5 entry" and "~3,000" exons.

required_discoveries_missed: CAMP4 RAP regulatory-RNA platform and the SYNGAP1 clinical analogue (~1.5-fold protein rise in NHP brain on biweekly intrathecal dosing) — the strongest mechanism-independent evidence that the magnitude goal is achievable

Enhancer-directed / eRNA transcriptional upregulation as a distinct mechanism, with its honest costs (targets not findable from sequence, contested eRNA biology, multi-gene enhancers, incumbent IP position)
The flux-vs-redistribution distinction: transcriptional upregulation increases pre-mRNA flux whereas poison-exon suppression only redistributes it, so only the latter needs a pre-existing event
Human nusinersen autopsy gradient with little drug in brainstem; the output instead claims brainstem is well covered
Named under-dosed compartments for this disease (deep cerebellar layers, interneurons in deep structures) and a requirement for primate coverage measurement before lead nomination
NGN-401 Rett high-dose cohort halt for hyperinflammatory SAE as the AAV safety anchor for the differentiation argument
Allele non-selectivity of the mutation-agnostic arms: boosting a mutant allele that makes stable truncated protein is not neutral, implying NMD-vs-stable-protein stratification
Correct reading of an absence: exclusion by a discovery pipeline's conservation/expression filters versus true non-existence, and the differing funding implications
First-experiment requirements: both heterozygous-female and hemizygous-male genotype contexts, more than one neuronal fate including interneurons, and gymnotic (reagent-free) delivery
Explicit arithmetic tying the waste fraction to a 1.5-fold goal (a 5% event recovers almost nothing)
summary: Strong on the two hardest dimensions: existence risk is actively tested and quantified, and the SCN1A trap is decomposed cleanly. But it misses the regulatory-RNA/enhancer axis and the CAMP4–SYNGAP1 analogue entirely, calls intrathecal delivery "largely solved", and most damagingly asserts a poison-exon-atlas absence its own appendix admits it never read — while that absence helps carry the kill criterion. Score 10/16; fails.
